summary: Frontend-only test for UTF-8 encoding bug fix in FileViewer.tsx (HTML analysis reports). Verified via a byte-level in-browser unit test that reproduces the exact base64→atob→TextDecoder pipeline used by htmlDecoded useMemo. The old buggy path (plain atob) was PROVEN to produce EXACTLY the corrupt sequences reported by user (âš , piÃ¹, Ã¨, â¬ for €, ð¢ð¡ for emojis). The new fixed path via TextDecoder('utf-8') applied to Uint8Array of byte-per-byte values PROVED to correctly restore the original Unicode (⚠, 🏢, 💡, è, à, ù, é, €, —). Fix is verified working. End-to-end UI render inside iframe could not be exercised because the test user has NO existing analysis HTML files in master-files → 'Analisi' tab (empty state shown), and login attempt with test@dalpastro.it did not persist across navigations — but this is a testing-environment limitation, NOT a bug. Backend already correctly encodes HTML as UTF-8 → base64 (confirmed at /app/backend/server.py:4047, meta charset present at line 4246). No regression risk to PDF path: FileViewer.tsx preserves atob() call in the PDF branch (pdfJsHtml, lines 122-124) unchanged because PDFs are binary, not text.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix in /app/frontend/src/FileViewer.tsx (htmlDecoded useMemo, lines 51-75) is correct and complete: (1) atob → binary string, (2) byte-per-byte Uint8Array conversion using charCodeAt(i) & 0xff, (3) TextDecoder('utf-8').decode(bytes). Fallback path uses decodeURIComponent(escape(bin)) which is a valid legacy trick when TextDecoder is unavailable.
Both HTML rendering branches (web iframe srcDoc line 195, native WebView html source line 218) correctly use the new htmlDecoded value instead of the raw atob().

PDF rendering branches (lines 122-124 inside pdfJsHtml) correctly keep raw atob() because PDF bytes must be treated as binary. Same for BillsSection.tsx#828, ShareSheet.tsx#104, QRScannerModal.tsx#483 (untouched per plan).

Backend _build_analysis_html at /app/backend/server.py line 4123 still includes <meta charset="UTF-8"/> at line 4246 and encodes with html.encode('utf-8') at line 4047 before base64 → no regression on backend side.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The htmlDecoded useMemo in /app/frontend/src/FileViewer.tsx is the ONLY entry point for base64 UTF-8 decoding of HTML content. Any future regression should be caught by re-running the browser unit test that encodes an Italian+emoji string via TextEncoder → btoa → then decodes with the pattern in htmlDecoded. Full E2E UI verification with a real analysis report requires either: (a) a seeded HTML analysis file for test@dalpastro.it in master_files collection with category='analisi', OR (b) an authenticated flow to upload a real bill PDF and wait for AI analysis to complete (~30-60s of Claude Sonnet call).
rca_of_issue: ROOT CAUSE: Prior code used plain `atob(dataBase64)` to render HTML analysis reports. atob returns a JS 'binary string' where each character stores a single byte via its code point (0-255). Passing that string directly to iframe srcDoc / WebView source={html} caused the browser/WebView to interpret the string as-is: sequences like the 3-byte UTF-8 for '⚠' (0xE2 0x9A 0xA0) were interpreted as 3 separate Latin-1 characters 'âš ', and similarly '€' (0xE2 0x82 0xAC) → 'â‚¬', 'è' (0xC3 0xA8) → 'Ã¨'. FIX: Convert the binary string into a Uint8Array (byte-per-byte via charCodeAt & 0xff) then decode with TextDecoder('utf-8') to properly reassemble multi-byte UTF-8 sequences into their true Unicode code points. VERIFIED: unit test with the string '⚠ Attenzione! più tardi, è possibile analizzare €100 — perché no? 🏢💡' round-trips perfectly through the new pipeline while the old pipeline produces exactly the corruption pattern from the bug report.
